title: Japanese Money Methods
note:
METHOD THREE — KAKEIBO. FIFTEEN scenes in this cut, not fourteen: the -en
     chapter runs to s73, because 6.14 and 6.15 are two US figures the -hi cut
     does not have (a card APR and the $400 emergency). The chapter map is taken
     from the VO line ids, never from the -hi row.

     Ground arc: warm on the book -> amber on 1904 -> neutral through the shelf
     and the blank page -> green on the method -> cool on why it was new -> red
     on the four categories and its held crop -> neutral through what survives ->
     green on the four and their order -> neutral on paper and the app -> red on
     what the set-aside line buys -> amber on the receipt.

     Archetypes: A A D A D A A A A B A A D B B, holding B across s72/s73 because
     the APR and the $400 emergency are one argument about the same shortfall.

     Three drawn layers: a hundred and twenty-one annual volumes with FOUR
     MISSING, the year cut into twelve with the saving coming off the top of
     each, and an app pointing backwards against a ledger pointing forwards.

s64.comment: 6.6 · A · PLATE · no role · cool — WHY IT WAS NEW. An inkwell and a nib.

s65.comment:
6.7 · A · PLATE · warn · red — THE FOUR CATEGORIES, which came later. The
     photograph is already money spread into groups; four drawn boxes on it are
     the rule-8 failure exactly. No kicker on this scene, verbatim.

s66.comment:
6.8 · A · PLATE · no role · neutral — SAY IT PLAINLY. Matched-frame hold on
     s65's photograph, tighter crop, ken direction continued from the shipped
     cut. Four marks added 2026-08-06. The beat is that the four categories are a LATER addition, and the word four appeared nowhere on screen across s64-s67 — a 29s run of four consecutive art-off A scenes. The count goes here and not on s65 because s65 is one of the storyboard's seven SOLO scenes (focal alone, no kicker); adding type there would break a device that is deliberately spread every 12-14 scenes.

     the frame.

6.14 · B · FIGURE · warn · red — OVER 20%. A card APR, cited to the Fed's
     own release. A mechanic under a car is the unplanned bill this line is
     about; the figure carries the rest.

s73.comment:
6.15 · B · FIGURE · target · amber — 4 IN 10, on a long receipt. HELD on B
     with s72: the APR and the shortfall are one argument. Nothing is drawn — a
     ten-cell grid here would be the HARA HACHI BU device saying something else,
     and a countable grid a viewer can read off is a statistic.
